claims.text: Spin-polarized DFT with many-body corrections, such as DFT+U or hybrid functionals, will predict ferromagnetic ground states more reliably than standard GGA-based DFT when exchange interactions are subtle.
Standard GGA-based DFT can underestimate subtle magnetic exchange interactions.
The target material has a delicate balance of electronic exchange interactions that may produce ferromagnetic ordering.
DFT+U and hybrid functionals provide an improved treatment of exchange-correlation or many-body effects.
Ground-state calculations should include spin degrees of freedom.
Converged k-point meshes, basis sets, and related numerical settings are required for the proposed comparison.
Exchange splitting and local magnetic moments mediate ferromagnetic order.
Refined exchange-correlation and many-body treatments improve the accuracy with which energy differences between competing magnetic states are resolved.
The advanced methods can capture stabilization of finite magnetic moments and the energetics leading to a ferromagnetic ground state.
The advanced method will predict a lower total energy for the ferromagnetic configuration than for non-magnetic or antiferromagnetic configurations.
The advanced method will predict robust local magnetic moments.
The advanced method will produce clear exchange splitting in the density of states.
Standard spin-polarized GGA-based DFT may fail to resolve the energy differences needed to stabilize a ferromagnetic state.
Predictions may depend on the choice and parameterization of the many-body correction, including the value of U.
The proposed methods may omit relevant effects such as spin fluctuations and non-collinear magnetism.
Calculated magnetic energy differences and moment magnitudes remain uncertain because of exchange-correlation approximations and incomplete many-body treatment.
